newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica shares slide on MCI concerns.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica shares slide on MCI concerns.

text.p: Shares in Telefonica de Espana underperformed on Tuesday, hit by a profit warning made last week by new partner MCI, and they could fall to 4,400 before finding support, dealers said.
"Telefonica is beginning to suffer from the (predicted) MCI losses through its alliance with BT," a dealer at Benito y Monjardin in Madrid said.
Shares in Telefonica fell 95 pesetas, or 2.10 percent, to 4,430 at 1115 GMT, while the IBEX-35 index of blue chips was down 91.99 points, or 1.28 percent, to 7078.22.
In April, Telefonica joined forces with British Telecommunications Plc and U.S.-based MCI, which are merging.

Last week, MCI, America's second biggest long-distance carrier, said losses due to heavy investments in local markets would be more than twice levels previously forecast for this year at about $800 million. It said it was finding it harder, more expensive and time-consuming to enter local U.S. phone markets.
The news hit BT shares immediately and have begun to weigh on Telefonica, dealers said.

Another analyst said last week's award of the state's 60 percent stake in Retevision to electricity firm Endesa and Italian firm Stet, which will soon compete with Telefonica in basic telephone services, had already been discounted.

"The share already has the future presence of Retevision completely discounted and the paper is coming out because of commentaries about a possible rupture of the merger process of BT and MCI given the (expected poor results)," an analyst at Renta 4 said.
Still, dealers expect the share to find support at 4,400.
"I think that the share could stop at around 4,400," the analyst at Renta 4 said.
